newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico overnight Cetes rate corrects lower.
newsitem.headline: Mexico overnight Cetes rate corrects lower.

text.p: Overnight Cetes dropped 160 basis points to 21.90 percent Wednesday in a technical correction from Tuesday's high pre-auction levels, dealers said.
"It's adjusting (downwards) in relation to yesterday. It looks more stable compared to yesterday's close when rates came under pressure," said one analyst here.
Cetes rates rose at Tuesday's auction, but to a lesser degree than expected. That, and the increased demand seen at the sale, should have a calming effect on the market, traders said.
Cetes rates rose in all maturities at the auction, with the benchmark 28-day rate climbing 113 basis points to 20.43 percent -- less than the 147 basis points anticipated by the market.
Dealers said Wednesday's market was less speculative than Tuesday's, but tight liquidity could push rates higher near-term.
"It depends on how the Bank of Mexico intervenes...what I would expect is that rates will remain stable, but with some upside pressure at the close," the dealer said.
"The market will continue to come under liquidity pressure, but without reaching the speculative levels that were registered mainly on Monday," he added.
In the medium term, the market will remain jittery ahead of mid-term elections on July 6 and the meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve policy wing the same week.
Bank notes and acceptances began the day at 22.70 percent following Tuesday's close at 24.15 percent. ((-- Fatima Escobar, Mexico City newsroom +525 728 9554))
